title: Rick & Linda — Tokyo, Oct 5 & 6
og_desc: Five slow-paced options for the two Tokyo days. Pick one for each day and tell me the numbers.

pre_sections.lead: Five options below. Every one of them is built the same way: taxi to the door, a seat at every stop, nothing that needs standing in a line. Read them, then send me two numbers — for example "Oct 5 = 3, Oct 6 = 2". That is all I need to start booking.
pts: Not every option works on both days
Tokyo museums close on Mondays, and one of them closes on Tuesdays instead. Each option says which day it can run. Options 1 and 5 work on either day.
Oct 5 starts at noon
You are at Toyosu at 5:30 that morning, and I have something until late morning. Lunch at 12:00 is the start of that day.
Oct 6 can start whenever you like
Say a time. Late is fine.
Cost
40,000 yen for the day, the same for either day. Entrance fees, taxis and meals are paid on the day as they come. Those are small on every option here — the biggest is about 1,500 yen a person.
If your back is worse that morning
Tell me and we cut it short, or cancel the day. No charge for a day we do not run.

sections.h: A garden on the bay, then the fish market
sections.lead: Hamarikyu is a 17th-century shogun's garden sitting between the skyscrapers and the water, with tidal ponds that rise and fall with Tokyo Bay. Paths are flat and there are benches the whole way. Then a short taxi ride to Tsukiji for food.
pts: Taxi to the Otemon gate
We are dropped at the gate. From there the pond is a few minutes on the level.
The tea house on the island

There is a tea house out on the water, reached by a wooden bridge. If it is open that day we stop for matcha and a sweet, sitting down, looking at the pond. I will confirm before we go — I am not promising it until I have.
300-year-old pine
One tree near the entrance was planted in 1709 and is held up by a forest of wooden props. It is the thing people photograph.
Tsukiji outer market afterwards

Ten minutes by taxi. This is the old market's shopping street — the wholesale part moved to Toyosu, but the food stalls and knife shops stayed. Most shops open on Monday and Tuesday. We eat sitting down, not standing in the street.

sections.lead: The Tokyo National Museum in Ueno holds the largest collection of Japanese art in the world — swords, armour, screens, Buddhist sculpture, 12th-century scrolls. It is the single best indoor day in Tokyo if walking is the problem, because there are benches in almost every room.
pts: Taxi stops at the front steps
No station, no stairs up from a platform.
We do one building, not five
The main building alone is a full afternoon. Skipping the rest is the plan, not a compromise.
Wheelchairs are lent free at the entrance
Worth knowing. Using one for two hours inside a museum is not a decision about your health, it is a decision about how much of the collection you get to see.
Garden and cafe on site
There is a cafe in the main building and a garden behind it, so the breaks happen without leaving.
Why not Monday
The museum is closed on Mondays. So is the Nezu Museum, and so are the Imperial Palace gardens. Monday is the reason options 3 and 5 exist.

sections.lead: The Suntory Museum of Art sits inside Tokyo Midtown in Roppongi. It is deliberately small — lacquer, glass, textiles, ceramics, one floor, quiet. Then a short taxi to Tokyo Tower and the main deck, 150 metres up, with seats and a cafe at the window.
pts: Lunch first, at noon
We start with a proper sit-down lunch at Midtown, then walk a few minutes indoors to the museum. Nothing outdoors between them.
The museum is one floor
That is why it is on this list. You can see all of it without deciding what to skip, and there is a tea room inside.
Tokyo Tower is a lift, not a climb
Taxi to the door, lift to the main deck. Admission is about 1,500 yen a person — I will confirm the exact figure before we go.
Stay for the light
If you want, we time the tower for late afternoon and watch the city switch its lights on. The deck has seating along the glass.
Exhibition and admission
What is showing at the museum in October decides the ticket price. I will check it and tell you before you commit to this one.

sections.lead: The East Gardens are the old inner keep of Edo Castle — the stone foundation of the main tower is still there, and you can stand on it. It is free, it is in the middle of Tokyo, and almost nobody hurries. Wide flat lawns, benches, one gentle slope.
pts: Taxi to the Otemon gate
We are dropped at the main gate and picked up at the same one. No station walk at either end.
The tower that burned in 1657
The keep of Edo Castle stood here and was never rebuilt after the fire. The stone base survives. It is a short ramp up and the view over the lawn is the reward.
The guard houses
Two original wooden buildings from the shogun's time are still standing inside the gate, and you can go in.
Rest house halfway
There is a covered rest house with seats and toilets roughly in the middle of the route, so the walk is split in two.
Afterwards, Marunouchi
Five minutes by taxi to the brick station building and a long unhurried coffee. Or straight back to the hotel if you have had enough.

sections.clock: Either evening — add to any day
sections.h: Dinner on a boat, sitting still for two hours
sections.lead: A yakatabune is a low wooden-roofed boat with tatami seating and a kitchen on board. You board, you sit, dinner is served course by course, and the boat moves down the Sumida and out into Tokyo Bay and back. About two and a half hours in which you do not stand up unless you want to.
nums: tell me and I will get it
pts: This is the least demanding thing on the page
It is also the one most people remember. Tempura fried in front of you, the Skytree and the Rainbow Bridge going past the window.
Boarding has steps
A short gangway and a step down into the boat. This is the one thing to be honest about with your back. I will tell the boat in advance and they will help you on and off — they do it every night.
Two operators run shared boats
Harumiya and Amitatsu both take parties of two on a shared boat. I will get you the price and the departure point once you say you want this.
It goes on top of a day, not instead of one
Pick option 1, 2, 3 or 4 for the daytime and add this to the evening if you want. Or do this alone and rest all day.
Tables have floor wells
Most boats have a sunken well under the table so your legs hang down, as at a normal chair. I will book one that does.

end.h: Send me two numbers and I will do the rest
end.lead: Oct 5 can be option 1, 3 or 5. Oct 6 can be option 1, 2, 4 or 5. If none of them appeal, say so and I will build something else — or we cancel a day, which is a perfectly good answer too. And tell me how your back is that week, because it changes how much I put in.

credit: Opening days, hours and admission taken from each place's own site, checked 23 Sep 2026. The items marked "to confirm" are the ones I have not verified yet and will not promise until I have. Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors.
